s: novice belongs to Gakkha (before being made to leave it)
q: Just as they carry off a young bird whose wings are not yet grown, so many unprincipled men will seduce a novice who has not yet mastered the Law, thinking that they can get him in their power, when they have made him leave (the Gakkha). (3)

s: Fifteenth Lecture, Called the Yamakas is a lecture
q: Fifteenth Lecture, Called the Yamakas.

s: creed is a pure, complete, unparalleled law
q: How can it even be imagined that he should be born again, who professes the pure, complete, unparalleled Law, and is a receptacle of the unparalleled Law?

s: control destroys Karman (as a thorn)
q: That which all saints value highly (viz. control), destroys the thorn (viz. Karman); practising it some have been liberated, and others have become gods.

s: control is valued by saints (highly)
q: That which all saints value highly (viz. control), destroys the thorn (viz. Karman); practising it some have been liberated, and others have become gods.

s: misery is escaped by wise man (through knowledge of the world's sins and avoidance of new acts)
q: A wise man gets beyond it who knows the sins of this world; sinful acts are got rid of by him who does not undertake any new acts.

s: Karman is acquired by new acts (not when new acts are avoided)
q: He who does not undertake new acts does not acquire Karman, and he verily understands (Karman); understanding it he becomes a Great Hero, who is not born (again) and does not die.

s: Karman is understood by Great Hero
q: He who does not undertake new acts does not acquire Karman, and he verily understands (Karman); understanding it he becomes a Great Hero, who is not born (again) and does not die.

s: Great Hero is a being without Karman
q: A Great Hero, who has no Karman, does not die.--As the wind extinguishes a light, (so he puts down) the lovely women in this world.

s: Great Hero is not born again
q: He who does not undertake new acts does not acquire Karman, and he verily understands (Karman); understanding it he becomes a Great Hero, who is not born (again) and does not die.

s: Great Hero does not die death
q: He who does not undertake new acts does not acquire Karman, and he verily understands (Karman); understanding it he becomes a Great Hero, who is not born (again) and does not die.

s: Great Hero has no Karman
q: A Great Hero, who has no Karman, does not die.--As the wind extinguishes a light, (so he puts down) the lovely women in this world.

s: Fifteenth Lecture, Called the Yamakas is called Yamakas
q: Fifteenth Lecture, Called the Yamakas.

s: men value Môksha (most, when women do not seduce them)
q: Those men whom women do not seduce, value Môksha most; those men are free from bondage and do not desire life.

s: men are free from bondage (when women do not seduce them)
q: Those men whom women do not seduce, value Môksha most; those men are free from bondage and do not desire life.

s: men do not desire life (when women do not seduce them)
q: Those men whom women do not seduce, value Môksha most; those men are free from bondage and do not desire life.

s: Môksha is valued by men (most by men whom women do not seduce)
q: Those men whom women do not seduce, value Môksha most; those men are free from bondage and do not desire life.

s: worldly life is turned from by men
q: Turning from worldly life, they reach the goal by pious acts; by their pious acts they are directed (towards Liberation), and they show the way to others.

s: pious acts direct towards Môksha
q: Turning from worldly life, they reach the goal by pious acts; by their pious acts they are directed (towards Liberation), and they show the way to others.

s: sexual intercourse is abstained from by men (men rich in control)
q: The preaching of the Law (has different effect) on different creatures; he who is rich in control, is. treated with honour, but does not care for it; he exerts himself, subdues his senses, is firm, and abstains from sexual intercourse.

s: heretics hold the view that gods put an end to misery (some)
q: Some (heretics) have said that they (viz. the gods) put an end to misery; but others (Gainas) have repeatedly said that this (human) body is not easily obtained.

s: gods are said to put an end to misery (by some heretics)
q: Some (heretics) have said that they (viz. the gods) put an end to misery; but others (Gainas) have repeatedly said that this (human) body is not easily obtained.

s: sage (Mahâvîra's interlocutor) knows past, present, and to come (all)
q: What is past, present, and to come, all this is known to the Leader, the Saviour, who annihilates the hindrances to right faith.

s: Tathâgatas are not born again again (because they engage in no undertakings)
q: How could the wise Tathâgatas be born again, the Tathâgatas who engage in no undertakings, the supreme, the eyes of the world?

s: Tathâgatas engage in no undertakings (wise and supreme)
q: How could the wise Tathâgatas be born again, the Tathâgatas who engage in no undertakings, the supreme, the eyes of the world?

s: Tathâgatas are eyes of the world (supreme)
q: How could the wise Tathâgatas be born again, the Tathâgatas who engage in no undertakings, the supreme, the eyes of the world?

s: Kâsyapa declares supreme condition (supreme)
q: And there has been declared by the Kâsyapa the supreme condition, by realising which some happy and wise men reach excellence.

s: Great Hero annihilates former works (without doing new ones)
q: A wise man who has gained strength (in control) which leads to the expiation of sins, annihilates his former works, and does not do new ones.

s: Great Hero does not do new works
q: A wise man who has gained strength (in control) which leads to the expiation of sins, annihilates his former works, and does not do new ones.

s: sage (Mahâvîra's interlocutor) annihilates hindrances to right faith
q: What is past, present, and to come, all this is known to the Leader, the Saviour, who annihilates the hindrances to right faith.

s: wise man are liberated Liberation (having come to the end and made manifest the end of the incomprehensible path)
q: There have been wise men, and there will be pious men, who having come to the end and made manifest the end of the incomprehensible path, have been liberated.

s: sage (Mahâvîra's interlocutor) knows creed (incomparable)
q: The annihilator of doubt knows the incomparable (Law); he, the expounder of the incomparable (Law), is not inclined towards this or that (heretical doctrine).

s: sage (Mahâvîra's interlocutor) expounds creed (incomparable)
q: The annihilator of doubt knows the incomparable (Law); he, the expounder of the incomparable (Law), is not inclined towards this or that (heretical doctrine).

s: sage (Mahâvîra's interlocutor) is inclined towards heretical doctrine (not this or that)
q: The annihilator of doubt knows the incomparable (Law); he, the expounder of the incomparable (Law), is not inclined towards this or that (heretical doctrine).

s: creed is a creed
q: On this or that (article of the creed he has) the correct opinion; hence he is rightly called a true (man); he who always possesses the truth, is kind towards his fellow-creatures.

s: creed surpasses world
q: In this creed which surpasses the world, (men) become perfected saints or gods, as I have heard; and I have heard that outside the rank of men this is not so.

s: sage (Mahâvîra's interlocutor) is a Saviour
q: Know this to be thus as I have told you, because I am the Saviour.

s: Sramanas gives up passions (that involve him in sin)
q: thus giving up every passion that involves him in sin, (such as) killing of beings.

s: Bhikshu is modest modest
q: He is a Bhikshu for this reason that he is not conceited, but modest

s: Bhikshu is obedient to Guru
q: and obedient (to his Guru)

s: Bhikshu sustains troubles and calamities (all)
q: that he sustains all troubles and calamities

s: Bhikshu practises conduct (with a pure mind)
q: that he practises with a pure mind the (prescribed) conduct

s: Bhikshu eats moderate quantity of food (given him by others)
q: and eats but a moderate quantity of food which is given him by others.

s: Nirgrantha is a religious ascetic
q: He is a Nirgrantha for this reason that he is single, knowing the absolute (âtman), awakened, proof against sins, well disciplined

s: Nirgrantha knows absolute (âtman)
q: knowing the absolute (âtman)

s: Nirgrantha is awakened awakened
q: awakened

s: Nirgrantha is proof against sins
q: proof against sins

s: Nirgrantha possesses Samitis
q: that he possesses the Samitis and equanimity

s: Nirgrantha possesses equanimity
q: that he possesses the Samitis and equanimity

s: Nirgrantha knows true nature of the Self
q: knows the true nature of the Self

s: Nirgrantha has renounced causes of sin (both objectively and subjectively)
q: has renounced the causes of sin both (objectively and subjectively)

s: Nirgrantha does not desire honour
q: does not desire honour, respect, and hospitality

s: Nirgrantha does not desire respect
q: does not desire honour, respect, and hospitality

s: Nirgrantha does not desire hospitality
q: does not desire honour, respect, and hospitality

s: Nirgrantha searches Law
q: but searches and knows the Law

s: Nirgrantha knows Law
q: but searches and knows the Law

s: Brâhmana has ceased from sinful actions
q: He is a Brâhmana for this reason that he has ceased from all sinful actions, viz. love, hate, quarrel, calumny, backbiting, reviling of others, aversion to control, and love of pleasures, deceit, untruth, and the sin of wrong belief

s: Nirgrantha endeavours to gain final Liberation
q: endeavours to gain Liberation

s: Brâhmana subdues senses
q: He who thus subdues his senses, who is well qualified (for his task) and abandons his body, is to be called a Brâhmana

s: Brâhmana abandons body
q: He who thus subdues his senses, who is well qualified (for his task) and abandons his body, is to be called a Brâhmana

s: Sramanas subdues senses
q: Such a man) deserves the name of a Sramana, who subdues (moreover) his senses, is well qualified (for his task), and abandons his body.

s: Sramanas abandons body
q: Such a man) deserves the name of a Sramana, who subdues (moreover) his senses, is well qualified (for his task), and abandons his body.

s: Nirgrantha subdues senses
q: Such a man) deserves the name of a Nirgrantha, who subdues his senses, is well qualified (for his task), and abandons his body.

s: Nirgrantha abandons body
q: Such a man) deserves the name of a Nirgrantha, who subdues his senses, is well qualified (for his task), and abandons his body.

s: Brâhmana possesses Samitis
q: that he possesses the Samitis

s: Brâhmana is not angry
q: is not angry, nor proud.

s: Brâhmana is not proud
q: is not angry, nor proud.

s: Sramanas is a religious ascetic
q: He is a Sramana for this reason that he is not hampered by any obstacles

s: Sramanas is not hampered by obstacles
q: He is a Sramana for this reason that he is not hampered by any obstacles

s: Sramanas is free from desires
q: that he is free from desires

s: Rishabha addresses sons (Rishabha's sons) (as a teacher)
q: (Rishabha said to his sons):

s: Brâhmanas leave rank (and suffer)
q: Even gods, Gandharvas, Râkshasas, and Asuras; animals who live on earth, and snakes; kings, common people, merchants, and Brâhmanas: they all must leave their rank and suffer.

s: Karman causes misery (through the fruit of works)
q: Notwithstanding their pleasures and relations, all men must suffer in due time the fruit of their works; as a cocoa-nut detaching itself from its stalk (falls down), so (life) will end when its time is spent.

s: heretics seek knowledge of truth (without crossing Samsâra)
q: See, those (heretics) who search for the knowledge of truth, but who do not cross the Samsâra, talk only about the highest good (without reaching it).

s: Sramanas is a ascetics (houseless)
q: Young and old people claim a houseless Sramana as their own, though he begs according to the Law, observes the rules of conduct, and performs austerities.

s: Sramanas begs according to Law (while houseless)
q: Young and old people claim a houseless Sramana as their own, though he begs according to the Law, observes the rules of conduct, and performs austerities.

s: Sramanas performs austerities (while observing the rules of conduct)
q: Young and old people claim a houseless Sramana as their own, though he begs according to the Law, observes the rules of conduct, and performs austerities.

s: monk renounce domestic life (despite family appeals and worldly temptations)
q: Whatever they will do to move his pity, however they will cry about their son, they will not captivate a worthy and virtuous monk or make him return to domestic life.

s: monk control senses (after giving up possessions and relations)
q: He who has entered the road leading to the destruction (of Karman), who controls his mind, speech, and body, who has given up his possessions and relations and all undertakings, should walk about subduing his senses.

s: destruction of Karman requires control (of mind, speech, and body)
q: He who has entered the road leading to the destruction (of Karman), who controls his mind, speech, and body, who has given up his possessions and relations and all undertakings, should walk about subduing his senses.

s: Law is proclaimed by Arhats (as commandments)
q: Follow the commandments which the Arhats have well proclaimed.

s: Arhats proclaim Law (well)
q: Follow the commandments which the Arhats have well proclaimed.

s: Karman is annihilated by austerities (through control and penance)
q: As a bird covered with dust removes the grey powder by shaking itself, so a worthy and austere Brâhmana, who does penance, annihilates his Karman.

s: Karman is annihilated through control (by a monk who abstains from actions)
q: If a monk who abstains from actions, suffers pain (for acts done) through ignorance, that Karman will be annihilated through control.

s: Samsâra is crossed by monk (through resistance to seductions)
q: Those who resist the seductions are placed on a line with those who have crossed the Samsâra.

s: pleasures are equal to diseases (in the view of virtuous men)
q: Those (virtuous men) regard pleasures as equal to diseases.

s: austerities are performed by monk (earnestly)
q: Knowing the truth, one should live up to it, seeking the Law, earnest in the performance of austerities, possessing the Guptis, being accomplished, one should always exert oneself, intent on the soul's benefit, and desiring the highest good (viz. liberation).

s: death affects living beings (young and old people and children in the mother's womb)
q: See, young and old men, even children in the mother's womb die.

s: absolute (âtman) has benefit sought Beatitude (through truth, austerities, and Guptis)
q: Knowing the truth, one should live up to it, seeking the Law, earnest in the performance of austerities, possessing the Guptis, being accomplished, one should always exert oneself, intent on the soul's benefit, and desiring the highest good (viz. liberation).

s: living beings owe Karman (their present form of existence)
q: All living beings owe their present form of existence to their own Karman; timid, wicked, suffering latent misery, they err about (in the Circle of Births), subject to birth, old age, and death.

s: living beings are subject to birth, old age, and death (in the Circle of Births)
q: All living beings owe their present form of existence to their own Karman; timid, wicked, suffering latent misery, they err about (in the Circle of Births), subject to birth, old age, and death.

s: birth, old age, and death affect living beings (in the Circle of Births)
q: All living beings owe their present form of existence to their own Karman; timid, wicked, suffering latent misery, they err about (in the Circle of Births), subject to birth, old age, and death.

s: Mahâvîra is a Arhat (reverend and famous native of Vaisâlî)
q: Thus spoke the Arhat Gñâtriputra, the reverend, famous native of Vaisâlî, who possessed the highest knowledge and the highest faith, who possessed (simultaneously) the highest knowledge and faith.

s: Mahâvîra is native of Vaisâlî (famous)
q: Thus spoke the Arhat Gñâtriputra, the reverend, famous native of Vaisâlî, who possessed the highest knowledge and the highest faith, who possessed (simultaneously) the highest knowledge and faith.

s: Mahâvîra possesses highest knowledge (simultaneously with highest faith)
q: Thus spoke the Arhat Gñâtriputra, the reverend, famous native of Vaisâlî, who possessed the highest knowledge and the highest faith, who possessed (simultaneously) the highest knowledge and faith.

s: Mahâvîra possesses highest faith (simultaneously with highest knowledge)
q: Thus spoke the Arhat Gñâtriputra, the reverend, famous native of Vaisâlî, who possessed the highest knowledge and the highest faith, who possessed (simultaneously) the highest knowledge and faith.

s: Gñâtrika is a great seer (knowing everything in the whole world)
q: Right conduct, &c., which has been taught by the Gñâtrika, the sage who knew everything in the whole world, has either not been learned or not been truly practised (by creatures now in distress).

s: Gñâtrika teaches control (as a sage who knew everything in the whole world)
q: Right conduct, &c., which has been taught by the Gñâtrika, the sage who knew everything in the whole world, has either not been learned or not been truly practised (by creatures now in distress).

s: living beings suffer for Karman (individually for their own deeds)
q: For in this world living beings suffer individually for their deeds; for the deed they have done themselves, they obtain (punishment), and will not get over it before they have felt it.

s: Kâsyapa has law followed Law (by those who abstain from sensual pleasures)
q: I have heard that sensual pleasures are said to have the strongest hold on men; but those who abstain from them follow the Law of Kâsyapa.

s: Law is proclaimed by Kâsyapa (as the Law of Kâsyapa)
q: I have heard that sensual pleasures are said to have the strongest hold on men; but those who abstain from them follow the Law of Kâsyapa.

s: Ginas commend control (as virtuous followers of the Law of Kâsyapa)
q: O ye monks, the virtuous (Ginas) that have been and will be, the followers of the Law of Kâsyapa, they all have commended these virtues.

s: Ginas follow Law (the Law of Kâsyapa)
q: O ye monks, the virtuous (Ginas) that have been and will be, the followers of the Law of Kâsyapa, they all have commended these virtues.

s: control is taught by Gñâtrika (as part of the highest good)
q: Right conduct, &c., which has been taught by the Gñâtrika, the sage who knew everything in the whole world, has either not been learned or not been truly practised (by creatures now in distress).

s: control includes Guptis (for one seeking the soul's benefit)
q: Knowing the truth, one should live up to it, seeking the Law, earnest in the performance of austerities, possessing the Guptis, being accomplished, one should always exert oneself, intent on the soul's benefit, and desiring the highest good (viz. liberation).

s: Beatitude is the highest good absolute (âtman) (desired through religious exertion)
q: Knowing the truth, one should live up to it, seeking the Law, earnest in the performance of austerities, possessing the Guptis, being accomplished, one should always exert oneself, intent on the soul's benefit, and desiring the highest good (viz. liberation).

s: living beings experience misery (as the result of their own deeds)
q: For in this world living beings suffer individually for their deeds; for the deed they have done themselves, they obtain (punishment), and will not get over it before they have felt it.

s: Third Lecture, Called the Knowledge of Troubles is a lecture (third lecture)
q: Third Lecture, Called the Knowledge of Troubles

s: relations press monk (to leave off control)
q: As a creeper encircles a tree growing in the forest, so his relations press him hard that he should leave off control.

s: attachment is a cause of sin (every attachment)
q: But a monk should renounce it; for every attachment is but a cause of sin.

s: monk should renounce attachment (as instructed in the Law)
q: But a monk should renounce it; for every attachment is but a cause of sin.

s: monk should not desire life (after instruction in the best Law)
q: He should not desire life, having been instructed in the best Law.

s: Kings and ministers of kings try to seduce monk (with pleasant things)
q: Kings and ministers of kings, Brâhmanas and Kshattriyas try with pleasant things to seduce a monk who leads a holy life.

s: Brâhmanas and Kshattriyas try to seduce monk (with pleasant things)
q: Kings and ministers of kings, Brâhmanas and Kshattriyas try with pleasant things to seduce a monk who leads a holy life.

s: monk lead holy life
q: Kings and ministers of kings, Brâhmanas and Kshattriyas try with pleasant things to seduce a monk who leads a holy life.

s: Sramanas have recourse to worldly sciences (when expecting want)
q: So some Sramanas, knowing themselves to be weak, have recourse to worldly sciences when they see that they will suffer want.

s: Sramanas should slip off pleasures (when exerting themselves for the soul)
q: A monk who exerts himself in a similar way, should slip off the ties that bind him to his house. Putting aside all undertakings, he should wander about for the welfare of his soul.

s: monk practise austerities (as part of mendicant life)
q: So a novice, who as yet has not suffered pains and is not yet used to a mendicant's life, believes himself a hero till he practises austerities.

s: Sramanas wander about Beatitude (for the welfare of the soul)
q: Knowing the beautiful Law, a wise and thoroughly restrained monk should bear all hardships and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: revilers are far from Beatitude (when reviling monks)
q: Some revile a monk who leads a holy life. But these revilers are far off from perfection.

s: heretics entertain false doctrines (when unworthy)
q: So say some unworthy heretics who entertain false doctrines, and who long for pleasures, as the ewe for her kid.

s: heretics are averse to Law (when unworthy and ignorant)
q: Some unworthy heretics, slaves of women, ignorant men who are averse to the Law of the Ginas, speak thus:

s: heretics are slaves of women (when unworthy)
q: Some unworthy heretics, slaves of women, ignorant men who are averse to the Law of the Ginas, speak thus:

s: Kâsyapa proclaims Law (as the governing religious teaching)
q: Following this Law which has been proclaimed by the Kâsyapa, a sound monk should carefully attend a sick brother.

s: Kâsyapa points out attachment (as a whirlpool dangerous to the ignorant)
q: There are these whirlpools which have been pointed out by Kâsyapa: the wise keep clear of them, but the ignorant go down in them.

s: monk know Môksha (when spiritually instructed)
q: Now a monk who knows (the truth about) Môksha should answer them: 'You speak thus, wavering between two ways of life (viz, that of householders and monks).

s: Môksha is a truth (known by a monk)
q: Now a monk who knows (the truth about) Môksha should answer them: 'You speak thus, wavering between two ways of life (viz, that of householders and monks).

s: monk should attend sick brother (carefully and according to the Law)
q: Following this Law which has been proclaimed by the Kâsyapa, a sound monk should carefully attend a sick brother.

s: monk should bear misery (until final liberation)
q: Knowing the beautiful Law, a wise and thoroughly restrained monk should bear all hardships and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: Beatitude is reached by monk (through enduring hardships and wandering)
q: Knowing the beautiful Law, a wise and thoroughly restrained monk should bear all hardships and wander about till he reaches final liberation.

s: great men reach Beatitude (according to ignorant assertions)
q: Some say that in old times great men, rich in religious penance, have reached perfection though they drank (cold) water (and ate fruits and roots).

s: monk receive begging (only what is freely given)
q: It is painful never to take anything but what is freely given, and begging is a liard task.

s: women are a temptation (difficult for the unwise to overcome)
q: As Vaitaranî, the river (of hell), is difficult to pass, so in this world women are to the unwise (a temptation) difficult to overcome.

s: women are related to sin (in the teaching of unworthy heretics)
q: 'As the squeezing of a blister or boil (causes relief) for some time, (and has no dangerous consequences), so it is with (the enjoyment of) charming women. How could there be any sin in it?

s: monk give up women (as part of established control)
q: Those who have given up intercourse with women and have left off adorning themselves, are well established in control, because they have renounced everything.

s: monk are established in control (after renouncing intercourse with women and adornment)
q: Those who have given up intercourse with women and have left off adorning themselves, are well established in control, because they have renounced everything.

s: begging is a difficult task (for monks)
q: It is painful never to take anything but what is freely given, and begging is a liard task.

s: Nirvâna consists in peace (through ceasing to injure living beings)
q: For this has been called the Nirvâna, which consists in peace.

s: living beings are not to be injured Nirvâna (whether moving or not, on high, below, or on earth)
q: He should cease to injure living beings whether they move or not, on high, below, and on earth. For this has been called the Nirvâna, which consists in peace.

s: monk should cease to injure living beings (whether moving or not, on high, below, or on earth)
q: He should cease to injure living beings whether they move or not, on high, below, and on earth.

s: monk should abstain from sin (by avoiding untrue speech and taking what is not freely given)
q: A monk who knows this, will live as a virtuous man guarded by the Samitis; he will abstain from untrue speech, and not take what is not freely given him.

s: Samitis guard monk (as they live virtuously)
q: A monk who knows this, will live as a virtuous man guarded by the Samitis; he will abstain from untrue speech, and not take what is not freely given him.

s: Samsâra is a flood (crossed by those who renounce everything)
q: As merchants go over the sea, so they will cross the flood (of Samsâra), where living beings despond and suffer pains because of their own deeds.

s: misery are caused by their own deeds (where living beings despond and suffer pains)
q: As merchants go over the sea, so they will cross the flood (of Samsâra), where living beings despond and suffer pains because of their own deeds.

s: Vaitaranî is a river of hell (difficult to pass)
q: As Vaitaranî, the river (of hell), is difficult to pass, so in this world women are to the unwise (a temptation) difficult to overcome.

s: weak men become disheartened misery (when unable to bear mendicant hardships)
q: All these hardships are difficult to bear; the weak return to their house (when they cannot bear them), like elephants covered with arrows (break down).

s: weak men return to house (when unable to bear hardships)
q: All these hardships are difficult to bear; the weak return to their house (when they cannot bear them), like elephants covered with arrows (break down).

s: relations are an attachment attachment (for monks)
q: He is held fast by his attachment for his relations.

s: relations try to persuade monk (to leave off control)
q: In this way (his relations) come to him, lamenting, and try to persuade him. Held fast by his attachment for his relations, he quickly returns to his house.

s: monk does not enter house (the woman's household) (when invited by women)
q: He should regard their words like wild rice, and should not desire to call at (their) house; for a fool who is bound in the fetters of sensuality will be subject to delusion again and again. (31)

s: monk does not commit sin (when maintaining religious discipline)
q: Restraining himself by the thought that these dangerous (pleasures) will not be to his benefit, a monk should abstain from women, and commit no unnatural crime. (20)

s: monk abstains from pleasures (when living single)
q: A monk, living single, should not fall in love; if he loves pleasures, he should again become indifferent. Now hear the pleasures of Sramanas, which some monks enjoy. (1)

s: monk bears austerities (while still required to avoid women)
q: Even a monk who practises severe austerities should avoid the company of women. (12)

s: monk wanders toward Beatitude (when his soul is pure and free from sins)
q: The hero (of faith) who has vanquished sin and delusion, has said all this. A monk, therefore, whose soul is pure (and free from sins) should wander about till he reaches final liberation. (22)

s: monk has state pure soul (when free from sins)
q: A wise and learned monk whose soul is in a pure condition (Lêsyâ), will abstain from doing work for others; in thoughts, words, and actions he will bear all troubles. (21)

s: women is a temptation (for monks)
q: Therefore he should avoid women, knowing them to be like a poisoned thorn. He is no Nirgrantha who without companion (goes into) houses, being a slave (to passion) and preaches (his religion). (11)

s: women uses clever pretences (to become intimate with monks)
q: With clever pretences women make up to him, however foolish they be; they know how to contrive that some monks will become intimate with them. (2)

s: women wears fine clothes (to attract monks)
